period_note: Standalone (solo) basis, from the bank's own 'Condensed Balance Sheet (Unaudited)'/'Condensed Profit and Loss Account (Unaudited)' (distinct from the 'Condensed Consolidated' statements printed earlier in the same filing) — chosen per this project's stated preference for Solo over Consolidated wherever both are available, and matching the basis of this bank's own 2021-2025 Q4/annual series. Paid-up capital is unchanged from 2020_Q3 (13,258,784,760): the FY2020 dividend was still awaiting shareholder approval at the time of this filing (per note 5.3: '*Dividend for 2020 will be presented for shareholders' approval in 22nd AGM of the Bank to be held on May 27, 2021'), so no restatement issue. Note 8 discloses a new 1%-of-net-profit 'Start-up Fund' appropriation (BDT 59,479,766, per SMESPD circulars 04/05 of 2021) taken out of retained earnings for FY2020+Q1 2021 combined — an equity appropriation, not a separate balance-sheet or P&L line, so not recorded as its own line item here (consistent with how dividend appropriations are not tracked as separate items elsewhere in this series). Balance sheet identity reconciles exactly: Total property and assets 388,196,967,499 = Total liabilities 341,742,478,448 + Total shareholders' equity 46,454,489,051. P&L subtotals reconcile exactly in raw Taka; independent per-line rounding to the nearest BDT million (as required by this dataset's unit convention) introduces a harmless ±1 million artifact between operating_profit/profit_before_tax/profit_after_tax when re-added (e.g. 6092-3070=3022 vs the reported operating_profit of 3023, because the underlying raw difference 3,022,575,544 itself rounds up to 3023). Solo Key Financial Ratios (note 6.3, annualized) give car_pct/roa_pct/roe_pct directly; no NPL% or cost-income ratio is disclosed anywhere in this filing. No COVID-19-specific commentary appears in this filing (unlike the 2020 quarters) — the notes instead attribute the YoY EPS increase to higher investment income on government securities, lower interest expense from rate reductions, and lower standalone operating expense (note 4.3), and attribute the NOCFPS decline to 'large deposit encashment by customers during 1st quarter of 2021' (note 5.3), with no asset-quality/moratorium disclosure.
